goal: Decide whether a value gets a UOR-ADDR content address, so two values with one meaning share a label and a malformed one gets none.

app.name: addr-admission
app.title: Address admission
app.purpose: Decide whether a value is labeled, refused, or labeled under its schema, from its format, whether it reached a canonical form and whether a pinned schema admits it.

fields.name: canonical
fields.means: whether the value reached its published canonical form

fields.name: schema
fields.means: what a pinned schema says, if one is pinned

meanings.labeled: a sha256 label of the canonical bytes
meanings.schema: the same label, admitted by the pinned schema

rules.why: README: each format is routed through its canonical form, JCS, canonical S-expressions, XML-C14N 1.1 or DER, and only canonical bytes are hashed
crates/uor-addr/src/schema: a failed admission predicate is AddressFailure::SchemaViolation
README: schema.org Photograph and Article and in-toto Statement v1 add admission without changing the label
crates/uor-addr/src/schema: the schema wrappers are JSON descendants, so no schema is pinned to another format

app.otherwiseWhy: canonical with no schema pinned: the sha256 label of the canonical bytes

properties.why: a label always names canonical bytes
schema admission exists only for JSON values

stakeholders.name: Integrator
stakeholders.text: Passes data across system boundaries and needs a label only for canonical, admitted values.

stakeholders.name: Binding maintainer
stakeholders.text: Ships the npm, PyPI, C and WebAssembly bindings and needs each to produce the same label byte for byte.

concerns.name: One label in every language
concerns.text: Every binding produces the same 71-byte sha256 label for the same value.

components.name: Language bindings
components.text: uor-addr-c, uor-addr-wasm and the npm and PyPI packages, which wrap the same Rust core.

components.name: Value producers
components.text: The systems on each side of a boundary that produce JSON, S-expression, XML and ASN.1 values.

threats.name: Non-canonical bytes labeled
threats.text: A value is hashed before reaching its canonical form, so two values with one meaning get two labels.

control.name: Canonical first
control.text: A value that did not reach its canonical form is never labeled, proved for every request.

threats.name: Schema pinned to the wrong format
threats.text: A schema admission is claimed for an XML or ASN.1 value, which no schema wrapper reads.

control.name: JSON schemas only
control.text: Only a JSON value is answered schema, proved for every request.

threats.name: Label collision
threats.text: Two values with different meanings get the same label.
threats.accepted: Different canonical bytes give different labels up to the SHA-256 sensitivity bound, which the README states as the guarantee.

quality.text: The Rust, C, WebAssembly, npm and PyPI surfaces produce the same label byte for byte.
quality.measureText: Bindings whose label for an example differs from the Rust core.
